faq.a: No, and the tool says so plainly. It's a rule-based engine using a built-in synonym and phrase dictionary of several hundred entries, not a language model. It swaps words and applies sentence rules, so output always needs human review for meaning and flow. It's meant for rephrasing your own writing, not for disguising copied text — which is still plagiarism regardless of the tool.

faq.q: What do the five modes actually do differently?
faq.a: Standard substitutes synonyms from the dictionary. Simple replaces hard words with easier ones (utilize→use, approximately→about). Formal expands contractions (can't→cannot) and swaps informal words for professional equivalents. Shorten removes filler phrases like "basically", "in order to" and "a number of". Expand inserts connective openers such as "Furthermore," or "As a result," between sentences.

faq.q: Can I control how much gets changed or protect certain words?
faq.a: Yes. The Strength setting (Light, Medium, Heavy) sets the probability each eligible word is replaced — roughly 35%, 65% and 95%. A "Protect words" field takes comma-separated terms (names, technical terms) that are never swapped. In the result, every changed word is highlighted; click one to pick a different synonym or revert to the original, and the output updates live.

After paraphrasing it shows words changed, the percent of the original altered, old→new word count, and a Flesch reading-ease score for both versions so you can see if it got easier or harder to read. It keeps up to 8 previous versions you can restore, and refuses runs under four words. Everything runs in your browser; state is saved locally under paraphraser_state and pr_hist.
